extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers / news consumers interested in wartime reporting
extracted.subtask_description: A frontline Associated Press newspaper dispatch reporting military movements, captures, air raids, and human-interest scenes from the North African / Cap Bon campaign (May 1943). The piece combines chronological dispatches, eyewitness observation, official communiqués, statistics, and personal anecdotes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chronological account
rubrics_metrics.description: “The following series of ... Associated Press correspondent, form a chronological account of the crackup of the German armies on Cap Bon during the last three days.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize the report as a sequence of dated dispatches/episodes so readers can follow the progression of events over time (examples in the piece: May 10, May 11, May 12, May 13 dispatches).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution and sourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use clear attributions: dispatches from Allied headquarters, Associated Press correspondent byline (Daniel De Luce), Middle East communiqués, local reports and quoted officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attribute key facts and claims to named sources (e.g., 'Dispatches told', 'Allied headquarters said', 'By Daniel De Luce', 'a United States staff officer said') to establish provenance and credibility; distinguish eyewitness material from official communiqués and delayed dispatches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eyewitness war correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: First-person observations and experiences: e.g., 'As an unarmed non-combatant war correspondent, I had rare experience when a captain of the famous Goering division stopped me on the road...'; 'I drove behind a string of armored cars.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include on-the-ground, first-person scene descriptions, encounters with combatants and civilians, and small immediacies that convey presence and authority (examples: interaction with German captain, observations of columns of prisoners).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of concrete figures and statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation of numeric data and totals: 'Prisoners totalled nearly 250,000,' 'about 30,000 prisoners,' casualty/loss estimates and counts of aircraft or tonnage of bombs dropped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply specific numbers (prisoners, casualties, tonnage of bombs, numbers of planes, distances) to quantify scale; when precise totals are given, indicate whether they are estimates and cite source if known (e.g., Allied headquarters, communiqués).

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic specificity and movement detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed place names, distances and movement descriptions: Cap Bon peninsula, Ste. Marie du Zid, Bou Ficha, Zaghouan, Medjez-el-Bab, 'ninety miles from the tip of Cap Bon peninsula to ... Medjez-el-Bab', 'twelve miles northwest of Bou Ficha'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear geographic references, distances, directionality and named towns/landmarks so readers can situate maneuvers and retreats spatially; use place names and measured distances to clarify advances, circuits, and lines of movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-interest anecdotes and personal stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of individual stories to humanize the narrative: rescued seamen hidden in a cemetery cottage, Williams the merchant ship captain, the cemetery caretaker tale, Italians giving wine to British, an Arab woman pointing out surrendering Italians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrate broader military events with short anecdotes about civilians, prisoners, individual officers or sailors to provide emotional color and reader engagement; these vignettes should be tied back to larger events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of official communiqués and military detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Citing formal military statements and unit identifications: 'Allied headquarters', 'Middle East air communique', unit names (British Eighth Army, Royal Tank regiment, Goering division, Sixth South African Armored division).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate official releases and specific unit identifications to anchor tactical/strategic claims; use communiqués for operational claims (e.g., bombing results) and combine them with correspondent observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vivid descriptive language and imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Evocative phrasing used to convey scene and atmosphere: 'big parade of defeat', 'dust-choked file', 'great blazes sprang up', 'grisly sight, spattered with human flesh.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use vivid, concrete imagery and memorable phrases to render battlefield scenes compelling, but balance sensational description with factual reporting and source attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual analysis of strategic implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpretive claims tying events to larger outcomes: e.g., 'A United States staff officer said that a collapse of German transportation was the chief factor which sped the capitulation of Nazi troops ...', assessments of morale and comparisons to Stalingrad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide analysis or reported assessments that explain why events unfolded (logistics collapse, morale breakdown, reinforcements on the way), citing officers or staff when making causal claims; separate reported analysis from correspondent's opinion.
